seo_title: Tim Hortons Case Study: Singapore Foodie Content | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read 12 months of Singapore cafe content for Tim Hortons: creators put 63% of their Foodie content into local discovery, while brands put 0%.
eyebrow: Creator case study · Cafe chain · Singapore
h1: Creators put 63% of Foodie content into discovery, Tim Hortons puts 0%
lede: SOMIN read 12 months of Foodie-directed content from Tim Hortons and six Singapore competitors, verified against the prior year, alongside a separate panel of four Foodie creators. Creators put 63% of their Foodie content into authentic local discovery and cafe experience; Tim Hortons and its competitors put 0%. The briefing turns that into three pillars, nine propositions and a 38-post Q4 calendar.
meta_line: A SOMIN creator briefing · Sep 2025 to Sep 2026 · Singapore · Foodies

stats.label: Creator Foodie content on local discovery

challenge.title: Tim Hortons faces 6 Singapore rivals that already own value
challenge.body: Tim Hortons competes for Foodie attention with Starbucks, Luckin Coffee, Tanamera Coffee, The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf, Koi and Paris Baguette Singapore. The category's centre of gravity is value and affordable indulgence, which competitors already own. The question was where Tim Hortons could stand out without out-shouting anyone.

approach.title: Brand, competitor and creator cohorts across 12 trend windows
points: Read 12 monthly trend windows from Sep 2025 to Sep 2026 and re-ran each against the same windows a year earlier (n=692).
Kept three cohorts separate and compared them by share, not raw counts: Tim Hortons (71), six competitors (939) and a four-creator Foodie panel (190).
Checked SOMIN's ads library for paid activity: no brand in the set ran visible paid content in the window.
Built a persona, tension, angle and story chain for each pillar, then nine propositions and 45 moment triggers.
Added a live 30-day topicality study of 85 panel posts.

findings_title: Where Tim Hortons stands on discovery, value and small joys

findings.title: Discovery is wide open
findings.body: Authentic local discovery and cafe experience is 63% of creator content and 0% for both Tim Hortons and its competitors. In the last 30 days, discovery still made up 39% of panel posts.

findings.title: Value is crowded
findings.body: Affordable indulgence rose from 11% to 19% of category content, verified against the prior year, but competitors own it. Novelty drops are the largest competitor theme at 20%.

findings.title: Small joys are Tim Hortons' own strand
findings.body: Everyday connection and small-joy indulgence is 27% of Tim Hortons' content against 14% for competitors. The briefing marks it partial: a strand to deepen.

delivered.title: Three pillars, nine propositions and a 38-post Q4 calendar
points: Three pillars weighted by opportunity: The Discovery Destination (45%), Small Joys, Shared (35%) and Fuel for the Active City (20%)
Three insight chains, each linking a persona, a tension, an angle and a story
Nine SOMIN propositions across product features, USP and promotion
A Q4 2026 calendar of 38 posts, three a week, with 12 lead posts from 1 Oct
A creative library of 108 concepts, 36 per pillar across the funnel

quote.text: Competitor absence is not permission. Each pillar rests on a real Tim Hortons asset.

outcome.title: Tim Hortons should claim The Discovery Destination first
outcome.body: The briefing ranks The Discovery Destination first: make each Tims store, drink and collab a place worth finding. No brand in the set ran visible paid content, so the whitespace pillar can be claimed without outbidding anyone. Small Joys, Shared and Fuel for the Active City follow as supporting plays.

faq.q: Who are the Foodies in this briefing?
faq.a: SOMIN classifies what content is about and who it is made for, so Foodies means content made for Foodies, not a measured audience. The primary persona is The Community Connector.

faq.q: Why is value not the recommended pillar?
faq.a: Value and affordable indulgence is the category's centre of gravity and competitors own it, so it is blocked. Whitespace needs creators high and brands low, which only discovery and aesthetic dining content meet.

faq.q: How reliable are the trend calls?
faq.a: Every directional status for the brand and competitor cohort was re-run against the same windows a year earlier. The creator panel only starts around Dec 2025, so its trends are labelled unverified, and the Sep to Dec 2025 windows carry low confidence.
